backgrounds: A single continuous set for the entire episode: a stylized stop-motion apartment kitchen/dining area at night. The kitchen occupies the left two-thirds of frame (wood-toned cabinets, white gas range with a glass teapot brewing, range hood with under-light on, hanging utensils and pans on a rail, coffee maker, knife block, cutting boards, a white fridge with magnets). The dining area is at right: a wood table with a hanging pendant lamp, upholstered dining chairs, a fruit bowl, and large multi-pane windows behind showing a dark blue night cityscape with lit windows. There is no scene change or camera relocation across the video -- it is one static-camera tableau with only minor reframing/zoom between shots.

lighting_notes: Warm, motivated interior lighting: a practical pendant lamp over the dining table and an under-cabinet stove light are the key warm sources, casting soft golden highlights on the wood cabinetry and the characters' faces. Outside the windows it is deep blue/near-black night, giving strong warm-interior vs. cool-exterior contrast typical of stop-motion sitcom sets. Overall exposure is fairly flat and even (little dramatic shadow play), keeping focus on character faces and small gestures rather than moody lighting.

visual_complexity_notes: The set is a single, moderately detailed but static kitchen/dining tableau -- more 'lived-in dense' than minimalist (many small kitchen props, hanging utensils, jars, window cityscape), but the camera never explores it; framing stays locked on the two characters so the environment reads as consistent background texture rather than something the story interacts with. This keeps visual complexity in the periphery while all comedic focus stays on the two puppet faces and the sight gag of the man's boxy, cloak-covered body area, which is a deliberate choice to center character expression and dialogue timing over set spectacle.
